observation: Verifier mechanics were no longer the main bottleneck; sibling exports lacked a standardized complete handoff package.
prior_belief: Another verifier increment might improve readiness.
intervention: Built a read-only conformance/readiness kit and mapped PROMETHEUS v0.5's declared attestation contract to Adapter v0.4 requirements.
measured_outcome: 32/32 focused tests and 6800/6800 adversarial cases before packaging; real PROMETHEUS contract alignment identified, runtime Transfer still absent.
evidence_quality: strong local mechanics plus sibling-owned declared-contract evidence; no authenticated runtime transfer
confidence_delta: higher confidence that the remaining blocker is evidence packaging/authority handoff rather than verifier feature depth
failure_surprise: Binary proof nodes broke naive JSON hashing; fixed with deterministic binary-aware canonicalization. A later RED was a test-fixture bug and was not counted as product failure.
reusable_lesson: Separate structural conformance, adapter readiness, authentication, and Transfer into distinct states.
invalidated_assumption: A design/checkpoint with attestation fields is equivalent to an Adapter-ready signed runtime export.
retry_condition: When a sibling owner emits a runtime export or Adapter v0.4 changes.
next_experiment: Real sibling export through Conformance Kit -> Adapter v0.4.
